stories.headline: IMD update: Third cyclone on trot developing over Bay by Monday
stories.title: IMD update: Third cyclone on trot developing over Bay by Monday
stories.summary: If the forecasts hold, this would be the third cyclone over the Bay of Bengal in quick succession during ongoing North-East monsoon season after severe cyclones Arnab and Murasu late last month
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Bay of Bengal is once again emerging as a potential breeding ground for a cyclone, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) flagging a fresh formation alert over its central parts by Monday evening.

A low-pressure area that lay over the south-east Bay on Friday is forecast to intensify into a depression by Sunday before rapidly strengthening in two successive stages over exceptionally warm ocean waters.
If the forecasts hold, this would be the third cyclone in quick succession during the ongoing North-East monsoon season.

Severe cyclones Arnab and Murasu had struck the Andhra Pradesh coast in rapid succession late last month, even as a developing El Niño over the equatorial eastern Pacific presented a seemingly contradictory backdrop to the unusually active storm season.

With the Bay continuing to host an active MJO pulse and oceanic conditions remaining favourable, the coming days will be crucial in determining whether the developing ‘low’ graduates into another powerful cyclone.
The immediate focus will be on how quickly it organises, how long it retains access to favourable atmospheric conditions, and, eventually, which stretch of the eastern seaboard it threatens.

The emerging system is drawing support from an active Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO), which has gained considerable amplitude over the Bay before preparing to resume its eastward journey towards the South China Sea.
The MJO is an eastward-moving pulse of enhanced cloud formation, thunderstorms and atmospheric circulation along the tropics.

When its active phase passes over a tropical ocean basin, it can create conditions conducive to cyclone formation by encouraging rising air, strengthening low-level atmospheric rotation and reducing the disruptive influence of vertical wind shear, or changes in wind speed and direction with height.
The MJO is therefore favouring cyclogenesis over both the Bay and the Arabian Sea, although this does not necessarily imply that El Niño is contributing to the process.
El Niño operates on a much larger canvas, altering atmospheric circulation, wind patterns, moisture availability and the distribution of tropical convection across ocean basins.
Its influence on cyclone formation is not uniformly favourable.

stories.headline: IAF to hold week-long aerial wargames near the LAC
stories.title: IAF to hold week-long aerial wargames near the LAC
stories.summary: A significant air exercise conducted by the Indian Air Force will take place in the Himalayas. It is scheduled to run from November 13 to 21, focusing on operations near the Line of Actual Control. Aircraft including Sukhoi-30MKI and Mirage-2000, along with transport aircraft, will participate in the drills. The exercises aim to enhance operational readiness in challenging high-altitude environments and validate military concepts.

stories.headline: IOC flags damage to India's Olympic image amid IOA election row
stories.title: IOC flags damage to India's Olympic image amid IOA election row
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: New Delhi: The International Olympic Committee (IOC) on Friday said the "reputation" of India's Olympic movement is taking a hit because of the "extremely regrettable situation" around the controversy-mired IOA elections and urged that the exercise be carried out fairly "without any external interference".

The statement comes after IOA (Indian Olympic Association) President P T Usha wrote to the IOC alleging that her failure to get elected in the Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOMs) panel was down to manipulation by other candidates under pressure from external forces.
Usha remains in contention for a second term as IOA head after being nominated by the Ice Hockey Federation of India for the December 5 General Body meeting in which the body's polls would be held.
The IOC said it is disappointed with the current situation.

"The IOC is very disappointed to note that, once again, issues and disputes seem to have resurfaced in the conduct of the IOA election process and in the implementation of the rules governing the IOA elections, despite all the efforts made over the past few years to establish a strong governance framework for the IOA in accordance with the Olympic Charter and the Basic Principles of Good Governance within the Olympic Movement.

"This extremely regrettable situation is, once again, negatively affecting the operations and reputation of the Olympic Movement in India," the IOC stated in a communication to multiple Indian media outlets.
India is among seven countries which are locked in a race to become an Olympic host in 2036.
And the power struggle in the IOA is not presenting a particularly rosy picture of the country's administrative set-up.
The IOC said it expects the IOA as well as the Electoral Officer in charge of conducting the elections to follow the Olympic Charter.

"The IOC has urged the IOA and the Electoral Officer directly responsible for the IOA election process to ensure that the IOA elections can be conducted in full compliance with the Olympic Charter, the IOA Constitution, and all applicable rules, in a free and fair manner and without any external interference," it stated.
(Except for the headline, this story has not been edited by Mathrubhumi and is published from a syndicated feed.)

stories.headline: Div Com Kashmir reviews Winter Preparedness, directs prompt Snow Clearance, stocking of Essentials in Remote Areas
stories.title: Div Com Kashmir reviews Winter Preparedness, directs prompt Snow Clearance, stocking of Essentials in Remote Areas
stories.summary: SRINAGAR, NOVEMBER 13: Divisional Commissioner Kashmir, Anshul Garg, today chaired a high-level meeting to review winter preparedness across Kashmir Division, emphasising coordinated efforts, timely response and adequate arrangements to ensure uninterrupted essential services during the winter season. The meeting was attended by Deputy Commissioners, Commissioner Srinagar Municipal Corporation (SMC), Director Airport Authority Srinagar, SSP Traffic Rural and senior officers from KPDCL, R&B, MED, PMGSY, ULB, BRO, NHAI, Irrigation and Flood Control, PHE, IMD, FCS&CA, Health, SDA, Police and other concerned departments. During the meeting, the Divisional Commissioner reviewed the snow clearance action plans of various agencies, including MED, R&B, PMGSY, ULB, SMC and BRO. He directed all agencies to ensure prompt snow clearance and clearly demarcate jurisdictional responsibilities to avoid duplication and confusion. He stressed optimal utilisation of available machinery and manpower and directed the concerned agencies to complete all pending stage contracts to strengthen the snow clearance mechanism. Concerned Chief Engineers and officers assured the chair that adequate arrangements are in place to ensure smooth, prompt and timely snow clearance on highways, major roads, streets and inner lanes immediately after snowfall. Reviewing winter power preparedness, the Divisional Commissioner assessed electricity demand and supply, availability of buffer stocks of transformers, transformer oil, DG sets and HSD in Gurez, besides the status of branch cutting. The meeting was informed that all districts have adequate transformer stocks while 80 percent of branch cutting has been completed. It was further informed that the average electricity demand in the Valley during winter is around 1,700 MW against an average supply of 1,300 MW, while peak demand during touchs to 2,400 MW. The Divisional Commissioner directed the Chief Engineer, KPDCL, to augment the capacity of workshops wherever required, complete the remaining branch-cutting work at the earliest, strictly adhere to scheduled power curtailment timings and ensure prompt repair of damaged transformers. While reviewing the availability of essential commodities in remote and snowbound areas, including Gurez and Karnah-Machil-Keran belt, the Divisional Commissioner directed FCS&CA to complete the advance stocking of LPG, petroleum products, rice and wheat within one week. He stressed that adequate stocks of essential commodities be ensured in all far-flung areas to prevent any shortage or inconvenience to the public during road closures. Taking serious note of delays in the commencement of winter air sorties in Bandipora and Kupwara, the Divisional Commissioner directed the Civil Aviation Department to operationalise the facility by December 1 to facilitate emergency transportation from remote and inaccessible areas. Regarding daily flight operations at Srinagar Airport, he directed the Director, Airport Authority Srinagar, to ensure timely dissemination of information to passengers and the general public about changes in flight schedules due to adverse weather conditions. The Div Com also reviewed healthcare preparedness across districts, including heating arrangements in hospitals, availability of essential medicines, deployment of medical staff in far-flung areas and the requirement for 4x4 ambulances. He directed NHM to provide 4x4 ambulances to the Directorate of Health Services Kashmir for their further distribution among districts, in addition to the SANJY ambulances. Emphasising proactive healthcare arrangements, he directed the Health Department to undertake comprehensive line-listing of expectant mothers and critically ill patients in vulnerable and remote areas. He further stressed their advance shifting to temporary shelters, wherever required, to ensure uninterrupted access to medical care during heavy snowfall and road closures. Reviewing the preparedness of the Jal Shakti Department, the Divisional Commissioner directed officials to ensure the uninterrupted functioning of all PHE schemes, including lift water supply schemes, and make adequate arrangements for the deployment of water tankers wherever required to ensure drinking water availability. He also directed the forest department to ensure adequate stocking of firewood at depots across the Valley. To strengthen interdepartmental coordination, the Divisional Commissioner directed all district administrations and departments to ensure round-the-clock functioning of their respective control rooms, including the Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC). He also instructed the appointment of nodal officers and sharing of their contact details to facilitate timely assistance, coordination and dissemination of information. Stressing the importance of timely weather-related advisories, Garg directed the concerned departments to ensure prompt sharing of information regarding weather and avalanche forecasts with the general public to minimise risks and safeguard lives. Meanwhile, he directed the Commissioner, SMC, to identify waterlogging hotspots across Srinagar city and ensure the deployment of adequate dewatering pumps to address any eventuality during the winter season. The Divisional Commissioner also emphasised the need for accountability and timely grievance redressal, directing all officers to properly document the time of occurrence of any issue and the response time taken by the concerned department to resolve it. During the meeting, Deputy Commissioners briefed the chair about the winter preparedness measures undertaken in their respective districts and highlighted critical issues requiring intervention and resolution. The Divisional Commissioner called upon all departments to maintain close coordination and ensure that all necessary arrangements are put in place well in advance to minimise public inconvenience and ensure the safety and well-being of people across Kashmir Division during the winter season.

stories.headline: The rise and fall of Nvidia's Jensen Huang
stories.title: The rise and fall of Nvidia's Jensen Huang
stories.summary: For more than a decade, Jensen Huang wore the same thing to almost every keynote: A black leather jacket, black T-shirt, black jeans. In March, under a heat advisory in San Jose, he still wore it, pacing the stage for two and a half hours without bringing on another executive to share the load.That leather jacket became shorthand for Nvidia, a company that, like its founder, seemed impossible to replace.On Thursday, it found out whether it could. Nvidia announced that Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and director, effective immediately. Chief financial officer Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO while the board searches for a successor.Huang resigned days after admitting to employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife. The New York Times reported his relationship with Alice Huang (not related to Jensen), a Megaspeed executive whom US officials believe is a Chinese intelligence asset, and later, a second relationship with an Nvidia executive. Hours after his resignation, Reuters reported a third relationship with another employee.Also Read: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO following two extramarital affairsIt is an abrupt end for the man who co-founded the company 33 years ago and built it into the first in the world to be worth $5 trillion.The Company and the FounderIn April 1993, Huang founded Nvidia along with Chris Malachowsky, an engineer at Sun Microsystems, and Curtis Priem, a graphics chip designer who had worked at IBM and Sun. They mapped out the company over meals at a Denny’s in East San Jose. Their bet was that 3D graphics would be the next big computing problem, and that video games would be the market to crack it.It nearly didn’t survive. The first chip, the NV1, flopped because it drew images in a way Microsoft’s software didn’t support. A deal to make the graphics chip for Sega’s Dreamcast console fell through. In 1996, Huang cut staff from 100 to 40 and bet everything on a single chip, the RIVA 128. By the time it shipped in August 1997, Nvidia had enough cash for one month’s payroll.Also Read: How the Jensen Huang controversy unfoldedThe RIVA 128 sold about a million units in four months. Nvidia went public in January 1999 and, later that year, launched the GeForce 256, which it marketed as the world’s first graphics processing unit (GPU). GeForce cards became the standard upgrade for PC gamers. Today, GPUs are the chips on which most AI models are trained and run.In October 2025, Nvidia became the first company ever to be worth $5 trillion. It peaked at around $5.8 trillion in early October this year. Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta and AI labs such as OpenAI all run their AI on Nvidia chips, as do Reliance and Tata in India.Also Read: Inside Jensen Huang’s family ties at NvidiaThe Immigrant KidBorn on February 17, 1963, in Tainan, Taiwan, Huang grew up in a household that prized education. His father was a chemical engineer; his mother, a teacher, taught her sons English using ten words she selected from the dictionary each day.The family relocated to Thailand when Huang was five for his father’s work at a refinery. Amid political unrest in Bangkok four years later, his parents sent him and his elder brother to an uncle in Tacoma, Washington.After his parents joined the brothers in the US, the family settled in Oregon. Huang finished high school at 16, became a nationally ranked table tennis player and worked as a busboy at Denny’s. He went on to study electrical engineering at Oregon State University, design microprocessors at AMD and then join LSI Logic, a semiconductor and custom microchip manufacturer.In the early 1990s, right before starting Nvidia, Huang was running CoreWare, a custom chip division at LSI Logic, and finishing a master’s degree at Stanford by night.Also Read: Meet Nvidia’s board of directorsLeadership StyleHuang ran Nvidia with an unusually wide span of control. Around 60 people reported directly to him, compared with the eight to ten typically found at many companies, yet he held no one-on-one meetings with them. Instead, executives discussed problems and received feedback together. He had little patience for information hoarding: “I don’t believe in a culture where the information you possess is the reason why you have power,” he has said.Nor did he rely on conventional status reports travelling up a management hierarchy. Employees across Nvidia were encouraged to email their “top five things” every week or two, sharing what they were doing, noticing or worried about. Huang read roughly 100 of these messages each morning. In his view, a company’s strategy was defined by what its employees did, not merely by what its CEO said. The emails gave him a way to see that work firsthand.His management style could be demanding and public. Nvidia, he has said, preferred not to fire people; he would rather “torture them into greatness”. He also challenged employees’ work in front of their colleagues. “You can’t show me something without me giving you some criticism,” he has said. “I’m always critical of everybody’s work so that I can help them be better.”Current and former employees have described seven-day workweeks, nights stretching to 2 am and meetings that descended into shouting, according to Bloomberg. Yet relatively few employees left. Stock grants vest over four years, and the company’s shares climbed nearly 4,000 percent between January 2019 and their June 2024 peak, making millionaires of many long-serving staff. After Nvidia crossed a $1 trillion valuation, attrition dropped to 2.7 percent from 5.3 percent the previous year.The flat organisation helped Nvidia move quickly, but it also placed Huang at the centre.All these years, Nvidia and Huang have been synonymous with each other. Huang routinely opened internal company all-hands meetings with the line: “Our company is 30 days from going out of business.” Clearly, the company—one of the most valuable in the world—is in no such danger now, and Huang still owns about 3.6 percent of it.But now, for the first time since the idea of Nvidia was formed at Denny’s, Nvidia will have to find out who it is without him leading the company.

opening: For more than a decade, Jensen Huang wore the same thing to almost every keynote: A black leather jacket, black T-shirt, black jeans.
In March, under a heat advisory in San Jose, he still wore it, pacing the stage for two and a half hours without bringing on another executive to share the load.
body: That leather jacket became shorthand for Nvidia, a company that, like its founder, seemed impossible to replace.
On Thursday, it found out whether it could.
Nvidia announced that Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and director, effective immediately.
Chief financial officer Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO while the board searches for a successor.
Huang resigned days after admitting to employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife.

The New York Times reported his relationship with Alice Huang (not related to Jensen), a Megaspeed executive whom US officials believe is a Chinese intelligence asset, and later, a second relationship with an Nvidia executive.
Hours after his resignation, Reuters reported a third relationship with another employee.
It is an abrupt end for the man who co-founded the company 33 years ago and built it into the first in the world to be worth $5 trillion.
The Company and the Founder.

In April 1993, Huang founded Nvidia along with Chris Malachowsky, an engineer at Sun Microsystems, and Curtis Priem, a graphics chip designer who had worked at IBM and Sun. They mapped out the company over meals at a Denny’s in East San Jose.
Their bet was that 3D graphics would be the next big computing problem, and that video games would be the market to crack it.
It nearly didn’t survive.
The first chip, the NV1, flopped because it drew images in a way Microsoft’s software didn’t support.
A deal to make the graphics chip for Sega’s Dreamcast console fell through.
In 1996, Huang cut staff from 100 to 40 and bet everything on a single chip, the RIVA 128.
By the time it shipped in August 1997, Nvidia had enough cash for one month’s payroll.
The RIVA 128 sold about a million units in four months.
Nvidia went public in January 1999 and, later that year, launched the GeForce 256, which it marketed as the world’s first graphics processing unit (GPU).
GeForce cards became the standard upgrade for PC gamers.
Today, GPUs are the chips on which most AI models are trained and run.
In October 2025, Nvidia became the first company ever to be worth $5 trillion.
It peaked at around $5.8 trillion in early October this year.
Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta and AI labs such as OpenAI all run their AI on Nvidia chips, as do Reliance and Tata in India.
The Immigrant KidBorn on February 17, 1963, in Tainan, Taiwan, Huang grew up in a household that prized education.
His father was a chemical engineer; his mother, a teacher, taught her sons English using ten words she selected from the dictionary each day.
The family relocated to Thailand when Huang was five for his father’s work at a refinery.
Amid political unrest in Bangkok four years later, his parents sent him and his elder brother to an uncle in Tacoma, Washington.
After his parents joined the brothers in the US, the family settled in Oregon.
Huang finished high school at 16, became a nationally ranked table tennis player and worked as a busboy at Denny’s.
He went on to study electrical engineering at Oregon State University, design microprocessors at AMD and then join LSI Logic, a semiconductor and custom microchip manufacturer.
In the early 1990s, right before starting Nvidia, Huang was running CoreWare, a custom chip division at LSI Logic, and finishing a master’s degree at Stanford by night.
Leadership StyleHuang ran Nvidia with an unusually wide span of control.
Around 60 people reported directly to him, compared with the eight to ten typically found at many companies, yet he held no one-on-one meetings with them.
Instead, executives discussed problems and received feedback together.
He had little patience for information hoarding: “I don’t believe in a culture where the information you possess is the reason why you have power,” he has said.
Nor did he rely on conventional status reports travelling up a management hierarchy.
Employees across Nvidia were encouraged to email their “top five things” every week or two, sharing what they were doing, noticing or worried about.
Huang read roughly 100 of these messages each morning.
In his view, a company’s strategy was defined by what its employees did, not merely by what its CEO said.
The emails gave him a way to see that work firsthand.
His management style could be demanding and public.
Nvidia, he has said, preferred not to fire people; he would rather “torture them into greatness”.
He also challenged employees’ work in front of their colleagues.
“You can’t show me something without me giving you some criticism,” he has said.

“I’m always critical of everybody’s work so that I can help them be better.” Current and former employees have described seven-day workweeks, nights stretching to 2 am and meetings that descended into shouting, according to Bloomberg.
Yet relatively few employees left.
Stock grants vest over four years, and the company’s shares climbed nearly 4,000 percent between January 2019 and their June 2024 peak, making millionaires of many long-serving staff.
After Nvidia crossed a $1 trillion valuation, attrition dropped to 2.7 percent from 5.3 percent the previous year.
The flat organisation helped Nvidia move quickly, but it also placed Huang at the centre.
All these years, Nvidia and Huang have been synonymous with each other.

Huang routinely opened internal company all-hands meetings with the line: “Our company is 30 days from going out of business.” Clearly, the company—one of the most valuable in the world—is in no such danger now, and Huang still owns about 3.6 percent of it.
But now, for the first time since the idea of Nvidia was formed at Denny’s, Nvidia will have to find out who it is without him leading the company.

Nvidia went public in January 1999 and, later that year, launched the GeForce 256, which it marketed as the world’s first graphics processing unit (GPU).

By the time it shipped in August 1997, Nvidia had enough cash for one month’s payroll.

The transaction was valued at ₹3,050 crore and was subject to regulatory and other customary approvals.

IntelliSmart, which was among India’s leading smart metering players, had a portfolio of over 2.2 crore meters across five states, including Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Assam.

stories.title: Bharti Airtel gets ₹2,400 target from Motilal Oswal on expected tariff hike
stories.summary: Siddhartha Khemka, Motilal Oswal Financial Services sees further upside in Bharti Airtel on a potential tariff hike and premiumisation, while NSE remains a long-term play on India's growing capital markets.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Siddhartha Khemka, Motilal Oswal Financial Services sees further upside in Bharti Airtel on a potential tariff hike and premiumisation, while NSE remains a long-term play on India's growing capital markets.

Bharti Airtel is positioned for further upside with a target price of ₹2,400, driven by an anticipated 10-15% industry-wide tariff hike by December or January, according to Siddhartha Khemka of Motilal Oswal Financial Services.
The telecom major's premiumisation-led growth strategy has already yielded continuous expansion in average revenue per user (ARPU).
A broader industry transition is expected to support this trajectory without relying on frequent rate increases.
"Overall, what we see is that there is a shift in the industry towards consumption-led pricing, which would sustain the long-term ARPU growth," Khemka said.
Airtel's capital allocation priorities—specifically investments in its fiber transport backbone and data centers—are also projected to generate robust free cash flow and improve return ratios.

Beyond telecommunications, the brokerage maintains a structurally positive outlook on India's broader capital market theme, highlighting the National Stock Exchange (NSE) as a primary proxy for this growth.
While BSE is expected to see a sharper near-term volume recovery, making it a preferred immediate play, NSE remains a strong long-term compounding story with a target price of ₹2,300.
The country's largest exchange commands a dominant competitive moat, holding a 93% market share in the cash segment, 99.8% in equity futures, and 75% in options.
Favourable cash modifications taking effect from December are anticipated to support a recovery in derivatives volumes.
Long-term growth is further underpinned by rising demat account penetration, digital onboarding, and increased participation from younger investors.
To strengthen earnings visibility, the exchange is diversifying into non-transaction recurring income streams, including colocation, data feeds, and clearing services.

stories.headline: Ministry Of Power Proposes Mandatory Energy Storage With Solar, Domestic Content Rules for Batteries
stories.title: Ministry Of Power Proposes Mandatory Energy Storage With Solar, Domestic Content Rules for Batteries
stories.summary: The Ministry of Power has proposed making energy storage a compliance requirement for solar and wind-solar hybrid projects. It has also proposed that batteries used in these projects meet domestic content norms, in draft amendments to four sets of competitive bidding guidelines. The ministry circulated the drafts and asked stakeholders to send comments by November 25, 2026, to nre.section-mop@gov.in. The amendments are proposals and have not yet been notified in the Gazette of India. Storage Becomes a Requirement Under the draft amendment to the solar PV bidding guidelines, procurement of solar power must comply with Central Government orders and Central Electricity Authority regulations that mandate installing Energy Storage Systems (ESS) alongside solar projects. Such storage must also meet domestic content requirements. The existing clause allowed solar procurement “with or without” storage. For wind-solar hybrid projects, the draft changes Clause 3.3 so that storage “shall” be added to the solar component of the project, instead of “may” be added as at present. It also removes the earlier listed purposes of storage: reducing output variability, delivering higher energy for a given capacity and ensuring firm power for a period. Localisation Extends Across Guidelines The Firm and Dispatchable Renewable Energy (FDRE) guidelines would require storage to comply with domestic content requirements under Central Government orders. The Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) guidelines would require tender documents to include provisions for domestic content compliance in BESS projects. The drafts do not specify the content thresholds. These are expected to sit in separate Central Government orders. Changes to BESS Bidding and Payment Security The BESS draft also revises the payment security mechanism. Under the existing framework, the Intermediary Procurer “will” collect a non-refundable Rs 5 lakh per MWh from battery storage developers for the Payment Security Fund. The draft says it “may” collect an amount “not exceeding” that figure, in instalments set out in the tender documents. Contribution to the fund would be optional for developers, and tender documents would have to say so clearly. Amounts collected would go to the fund set up by the Government of India for the Intermediary Procurer. The draft also restates the bidding parameters for BESS capacity procurement. Bids may be invited on an availability-based fixed charge or annuity, expressed in rupees per kW or MW per year or month, and/or on the quantum of Viability Gap Funding (VGF) a bidder requires against a pre-specified tariff. The minimum term of the BESS power agreement is envisaged at eight years, extendable as needed. Background The solar guidelines were notified on July 28, 2023, the wind-solar hybrid guidelines on August 21, 2023 and the FDRE guidelines on June 9, 2023. All three were later amended in November 2023, February 2024 and February 2025. The BESS guidelines date to March 10, 2022, and were amended on May 30, 2022. Draft Guidelines Leave Storage and Domestic Content Questions Unanswered The Ministry of Power’s proposed amendments make energy storage a compliance requirement for solar and wind-solar hybrid projects, but leave the details of the mandate to separate orders and regulations that the drafts do not name. They also do not say how much storage will be required, or for what duration. The solar clause itself carries an internal tension: the base text still allows projects “with or without” storage, while the new proviso mandates it wherever central orders apply. Domestic content is the other open question. All four drafts require storage to comply with such norms, yet none defines what counts as domestic, whether cells, battery packs or the entire system, or sets a threshold. Industry may also seek clarity on transition arrangements for tenders already issued, and on how mandatory storage and localisation will affect bid tariffs. With comments due by November 25, the 15-day window for four sets of guidelines may prompt calls for an extension.

stories.headline: India finish youth olympics with 10 medals and two boxing golds
stories.title: India finish youth olympics with 10 medals and two boxing golds
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 13 : India signed off from the 2026 Summer Youth Olympic Games in Dakar with 10 medals, including two gold, three silver and five bronze, marking the country's second-best performance in the history of the competition. India's medal-winning campaign spanned seven disciplines, with five Khelo India Athletes among the medallists. They included Tanvi Patri (Badminton), Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada (Judo), Shourya Ambure (Athletics), Gunjan (Boxing) and Tirthank Pegu (Swimming). Nine of India's 17 athletes returned with medals, while swimmer Dhinidhi Desinghu created history by becoming the first Indian athlete to win two medals in a single edition of the Youth Olympic Games. India's 10-medal tally was surpassed only by its 13-medal performance at the 2018 Youth Olympics. Boxing emerged as India's biggest success story, with Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei winning gold in the boys' 50kg category and Gunjan claiming the top podium finish in the girls' 48kg category. The two victories gave India its first-ever gold medals in boxing at the Youth Olympic Games and marked the country's first boxing gold double at the competition. With two gold medals, India also recorded its second-highest gold medal tally in a single edition of the Youth Olympic Games. The campaign also witnessed several historic achievements across other disciplines. Shourya Ambure became the first Indian athlete to win an athletics medal at the Youth Olympic Games, claiming bronze in the girls' 100m hurdles. Taniya secured silver in girls' freestyle 75kg beach wrestling, giving India its first-ever medal in the discipline at the competition. India also registered its first medals in swimming and Wushu at the Youth Olympics. Swimming was the country's most productive sport at the Games, contributing three medals. Dhinidhi Desinghu won bronze medals in the girls' 100m and 200m freestyle events, becoming the first Indian athlete to win two medals in a single edition of the competition. Tirthank Pegu added another bronze in the boys' 200m butterfly event. In badminton, Tanvi Patri won silver in the girls' singles event, becoming the first Indian woman to win a badminton medal at the Youth Olympic Games. Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada secured silver in the girls' 63kg judo category. Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu, a camper at the Sports Authority of India (SAI) National Centre of Excellence (NCOE) in Imphal, won bronze in the girls' Changquan combined event, giving India its first-ever Wushu medal at the Youth Olympics. India's 10 medals came across seven of the 11 sports in which the country competed, underlining the progress made by its young athletes across disciplines. India's medallists at Dakar Youth Olympic Games 2026: Gold: 1. Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei – Boxing (Boys' 50kg) 2. Gunjan – Boxing (Girls' 48kg) Silver: Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada – Judo (Girls' 63kg) Tanvi Patri – Badminton (Girls' Singles) Taniya – Beach Wrestling (Girls' Freestyle 75kg) Bronze: Dhinidhi Desinghu – Swimming (Girls' 100m Freestyle) Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu – Wushu (Girls' Changquan Combined) Dhinidhi Desinghu – Swimming (Girls' 200m Freestyle) Tirthank Pegu – Swimming (Boys' 200m Butterfly) Shourya Ambure – Athletics (Girls' 100m Hurdles) (IANS)
